heading: Beyond trends,

paragraphs: The same procedure does not suit everyone. We begin by reading the proportions of the face and body before discussing a surgical method.
Our standard is not what looks most fashionable today, but what can remain natural years from now. Consultation, treatment, recovery, and follow-up are one connected process.

process.heading: How a consultation unfolds
process.description: From your first message to the day you return to your routine, here is what each stage looks at and what you decide.

steps.title: Getting in touch
steps.description: Reach us by phone, KakaoTalk, or the online form, whichever is easiest. Nothing has to be decided at this stage.

steps.title: One-to-one specialist consultation
steps.description: We review your facial and body proportions together and talk through the impression you want and what is realistically possible.

steps.title: Planning and confirmation
steps.description: We summarise the surgical approach, the expected recovery period, and the cost. Take the time you need before deciding.
steps.note: Same day or a second visit

steps.title: Surgery and treatment
steps.description: Pre-operative testing and an anaesthesia review come first. The specialist who consulted with you performs the procedure.

steps.title: Follow-up and aftercare
steps.description: We check your recovery against a set schedule and adjust the timing of your visits where it is needed.

process.notice: This outline describes the general flow. The stages and the time each one takes may differ depending on the procedure and your individual condition.

faq.heading: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: The questions we are asked most often before a consultation. If yours is not answered here, please raise it with us directly.

items.question: Do I need an appointment?
items.answer: Walk-in consultations are possible, but the wait can be long. Contact us in advance and we will hold a time that suits you.

items.question: Is there a fee for a consultation?
items.answer: The consultation itself is free of charge. If an examination or treatment is needed alongside it, we explain that before proceeding.

items.question: What should I bring to a consultation?
items.answer: Photographs of the look you have in mind and any previous medical records are helpful. Please also tell us about any medication you are taking.

items.question: What kind of anaesthesia is used?
items.answer: Local or sedation anaesthesia is used depending on the extent of the procedure. The method and its precautions are explained during the pre-operative consultation.

items.question: Can I consult about surgery performed at another clinic?
items.answer: Yes. We need to know when and how the earlier surgery was performed, so please bring any related records with you.

items.question: Does someone need to accompany me on the day?
items.answer: Depending on the anaesthesia, you may need someone with you when you leave. We confirm this in advance once the surgical plan is set.

items.question: How long until I can return to my routine?
items.answer: This varies considerably with the procedure and with individual recovery. We set out an expected timeline during your consultation.

items.question: When do I come back after surgery?
items.answer: You return on a set schedule for suture removal and progress checks. That schedule is shared with you before surgery.

items.question: How are swelling and bruising managed?
items.answer: You receive written aftercare instructions and precautions immediately after surgery, with further guidance as your recovery progresses.

items.question: How is the cost determined?
items.answer: It depends on the extent and method of the procedure and the type of anaesthesia. We summarise the full amount once the plan is confirmed in consultation.

items.question: Can I get a price without a consultation?
items.answer: An exact figure requires an assessment first. We can give an approximate range by phone or messenger.

items.question: Are there additional costs after surgery?
items.answer: Scheduled progress checks are included in the plan. If further treatment or testing is needed, we explain that before going ahead.

faq.notice: These answers describe general clinical practice and do not replace a diagnosis or prescription. Outcomes vary from person to person, so please consult a specialist directly.
